Crowd Work is one of Comedy’s most fun and risky tools. Used effectively it can elevate an average set to a smash. Or it can make you look unprepared and unprofessional.

Learn about the how’s, why’s, and when’s of doing crowd work from a pro-comic. Take in the theory and then practice it yourself in the room to start building a new comedy muscle in this hands-on workshop.

Whether you are creating a connection, establishing power, setting up a bit, or dealing with a heckler – there’s plenty of places on and off the stage for good crowd work.

Brendon Green has been doing comedy for over 15 years, and has talked with audiences all over the world. He has been (or currently is) the audience warm up act for Taskmaster NZ, Guy Montgomery’s Guy Mont-Spelling Bee, 7 Days, Dancing With The Stars, The Project, Paddy Gower Has Issues, Have You Been Paying Attention, plus a bunch of other shows. Getting Started in Standup - Wellington
Have you always wanted to try stand-up comedy but don’t know how to start?

Comedian and writer Neil Thornton brings you a fun, low-pressure comedy workshop.

Sign up here: https://www.nzcomedyschool.com/enroll

Suggested koha: $20

Everything you need to know to get a mic in your face:
-generating ideas
-joke writing
-effective delivery
-where and how to get practice
-how to avoid many common mistakes new performers make.

In addition to his career as a stand-up comedian, Neil Thornton has been teaching for more than 25 years. He earned his BA in English from Carnegie Mellon University and his MFA in writing from the University of New Orleans.

He published fiction and essays in several literary journals and magazines and taught college English for 9 years, running classes in Creative Writing, Composition, Creative Nonfiction, Technical Writing, and Managerial Communication.

After moving to New York City in 2007, Neil became a working stand-up comic, performing everywhere from major comedy clubs to seedy dive bars in Washington D.C., Provincetown, Fire Island, and the Poconos. More recently, what was supposed to be a six-month adventure in New Zealand has turned into a permanent home.

Since then, Neil has made a big impact on the New Zealand comedy circuit. He has toured up and down the country and all over the world, entertaining audiences with his battles of understanding Kiwi culture and finding his own identity. He's a regular at The Classic in Auckland, and appeared in the TV3 comedy special "After Hours."

Neil now teaches from Wellington, New Zealand, where he continues to write, perform standup, and raise two giant Alaskan Malamutes.

Date my Queer Mate
We are back because you loved it so much last time!

Looking for a date? Who better to sing your praises than your mate?

Join us for the global phenomenon Date My Mate! But this time it’s QUEER! Come and flirt, mix, pash and dance!
﻿
The Good Sex Project Podcast and Emily Writes welcome you to Date My (Queer) Mate. This is a queer, trans inclusionary FLINTAQ* event. Equal parts comedy show, PowerPoint night, and match-making good time - come and mingle with dates and mates!
﻿
5pm doors open
6pm presentations start
﻿
How it works
Upon arrival, you grab a badge to say if you're looking for dates OR mates.
﻿
Friends take the stage with a 3-5 minute slide deck to pitch their mates. If you're interested in pitching a mate, please register here:

YOU MUST REGISTER TO BE IN WITH A CHANCE TO PRESENT
﻿
No stress if you aren't keen to pitch or be pitched; we need many audience babes - that's you!
﻿
Once pitches are done, there will be time to mingle and meet.
﻿
FLINTAQ* = FLINTA is a German acronym that stands for "Frauen, Lesben, Intergeschlechtliche, nichtbinäre, trans und agender Personen", meaning women, lesbians, intersex, non-binary, trans and agender people. The asterisk represents all non-binary gender identities. To explicitly include queer individuals, the term FLINTAQ is sometimes used. This includes bisexual and pansexual folks!

This event is ENM friendly.
﻿

long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black and White (Public Talk - Dr Malcolm Doidge)
Dr Malcolm Doidge presents his 360-degree time-lapse photography project, captured in Futuna Chapel across the 2023–2024 equinoxes and solstices. A short film of the project will be screened, followed by insights into the digital processes behind its creation.

About the speaker
After completing his studies at the University of Canterbury School of Fine Art in 1984, Malcolm Doidge worked for the New Zealand Correspondence School as an illustrator. He received his first commission from Lincoln College (now University), producing the work 'Ascent' in 1984.

In more recent years Doidge has taught Creative Technologies at Weltec (Wellington) and completed a Doctor of Philosophy, Inside Arcadia: An immersive virtual phantasmagoria. His degree was conferred by Massey University, Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, in 2022.

His work has been recognised by several awards including the Wallace Art Award (2004, 2006, 2009, 2013 and 2016), the Visa Gold Art Award (1998) and he was the premier award winner in the NCC Art Award in 2002.

About this Event



🍇 Bienvenue en Charente ! Tucked away in south-west France, this is the land of cognac, comic books and some of the prettiest villages in the country, and most visitors drive straight past it.

Join Thomas for a fun and immersive workshop (en français !) and set off on a journey through the département, one stop at a time. You'll wander the villages of Aubeterre-sur-Dronne and Verteuil-sur-Charente, then head through the vineyards to Cognac. And you'll explore Angoulême, the medieval city on the ramparts that became the world capital of la bande dessinée 💥

And of course, no trip to Charente is complete without its specialities: cognac, pineau, la galette charentaise and the famous cagouilles. Don't know what those are? Come and find out 🐌

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1-hour gong bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

**THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Gong baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:

-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)

If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first.

Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

long_description:
AI and Authoritarianism: Panel Discussion
Pōneke Anti-Fascist Coalition and Critical Signals invites you to a panel event about the various ways that Generative AI can be, and is being, deployed to advance authoritarianism. Panellists Aditi Tiwari, Dr Mike Joy, Lelitu and Anne Campbell will talk about the authoritarian implications of Generative AI in relation to topics that are important to them, including data sovereignty, workers rights, education, environmental harm, and militarism and surveillance. This will be followed by an open discussion where anyone is free to ask questions, share their own observations about GenAI and authoritarianism, or put forward ideas for resisting this technology.

Please register here for tickets https://buytickets.at/criticalsignals/2462201/share/2426de0105228d20791c50469e358ffa

More about the panellists:
Aditi Tiwari (she/her) on Data Sovereignty and Indigenous Data Sovereignty:
Aditi is a Master of Professional Business Analysis student at Victoria University of Wellington, whose research explores digital leadership, AI governance and Indigenous data sovereignty in AI-enabled public sector systems through a Te Tiriti o Waitangi lens. Her work examines the intersections of emerging technologies, power, accountability and data sovereignty, particularly how decisions about the collection, ownership and use of data can reinforce existing structural inequalities. As a first-generation migrant and community advocate, Aditi brings both academic and lived perspectives to conversations about digital equity, representation and the concentration of power in technological systems. She is particularly interested in how AI governance can uphold Indigenous rights, strengthen democratic accountability and ensure communities retain meaningful control over their data and digital futures.

Lelitu (it/is) on GenAI and Workers' Rights:
Lelitu is a software engineer in Te Whanganui A Tara with a decade of experience in commercial software development. Its experience has been radicalising at times, driving home the importance of workers rights and protections. It is extremely concerned about how bosses are driving very anti worker practices around the use and adoption of LLMs in the workplace.

Dr Mike Joy (he/him) on Environmental implications of AI:
Dr Mike Joy is a Senior Research Fellow in the School of Geography, Environment and Earth Sciences at Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington, and an outspoken advocate for environmental protection in New Zealand. His research includes ecological modelling, freshwater bioassessment, environmental policy development, biophysical limits to growth, and the role of energy in society. He has provided expert evidence for high court, environment court and Waitangi Tribunal cases, and has communicated extensively about the influence of vested interests on environmental policy. Mike is the recipient of numerous awards for his research and science communication, including the Morgan Foundation's inaugural River Voice Award, the inaugural NZ Universities Critic and Conscience award, an Ecology in Action award from the NZ Ecological Society, the Charles Fleming Award for environmental achievement, and the Callaghan Medal for science communication from the Royal Society of New Zealand.

Anne Campbell (they/she) on GenAI's impacts on education, learning and the psychological wellbeing of children and users:
Anne is a writer and local activist in Te Whanganui A Tara who has recently started working in primary education. Many of the tamariki they work with have independently expressed a wide range of concerns about AI, increasing her interest in how digital technologies affect learning and emotional development.

Valerie Morse (she/her) on AI, militarism and surveillance:
Valerie is a peace activist, gardener and writer working to oppose the expansion of military spending, the use of AI in the military and deployment of lethal autonomous systems.

long_description:
Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change (November)
Helping managers and people leaders in New Zealand regulatory agencies navigate AI-enabled change with confidence.

About this Event


Programme Details
Dates: Wednesday, 18 November & Thursday, 19 November
Time: 9:00 am – 1:00 pm daily (2-day interactive workshop)
Location: MartinJenkins, Wellington
Investment: $1,400 + GST per seat
Capacity: Strictly limited to 10 participants to ensure an interactive, small-group experience.
Facilitators: Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths

The Leadership Challenge

Artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities across the public sector, but technology is only part of the story. For many leaders, the immediate challenge is helping people adapt. Teams are asking questions about changing work practices, emerging capabilities, workforce impacts, and what these changes mean for their day-to-day roles.

Leaders are increasingly expected to communicate clearly, manage uncertainty, respond to concerns, maintain engagement, and support learning while organisational approaches continue to evolve.

Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change has been designed to help people leaders meet these challenges. Rather than teaching AI tools, the programme focuses on the practical leadership skills needed to guide teams through change.


Who This Programme Is For

This programme is designed specifically for people leaders within New Zealand regulatory agencies and public sector bodies, including:

Managers
Team leaders
Anyone responsible for supporting people through organisational change

No technical background or AI expertise is required.


What Participants Will Gain

By the end of the programme, participants will be better equipped to:

Understand the unique people impacts of AI-enabled change
Recognise and address common concerns and resistance
Lead teams through uncertainty and ambiguity
Build confidence and trust during periods of change
Communicate effectively about emerging technologies and organisational shifts
Support adaptation, continuous learning, and experimentation
Apply practical leadership approaches immediately within their own teams





Programme Structure
Day 1: Understanding the change and leading through uncertainty

Wednesday, 18 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

Leaders explore the people impacts of AI-enabled change and their role in guiding teams through it. They will understand how to assess readiness, communicate honestly, and build psychological safety in regulatory and public sector settings.


What will be covered
The leadership context for AI-driven change
How people respond to change and uncertainty
Change readiness and leadership responsibilities
Building trust through clear, credible communication
Crafting messages leaders can use with their teams
Reflecting on risks and opportunities in own context

Day 2: Engaging teams and turning change into action

Thursday, 19 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

The focus shifts from understanding change to leading it. This will include sustaining engagement and motivation, applying frameworks to real situations, and leaving with a practical plan for adoption.


What will be covered
Team engagement and motivation during change
Applying practical change leadership frameworks
Responding to resistance, fear and scepticism
Supporting learning and capability development
Safe experimentation and responsible adoption
Pulse checks, action planning and next steps





Learning Approach

This is a highly interactive, small-group programme built around:

Facilitated discussion
Real public sector examples
Practical leadership tools and frameworks
Small-group exercises and peer learning
Application to participants' own workplace contexts

Participants are encouraged to bring current challenges and opportunities from their own organisations.


Why This Programme Is Different

Many AI learning programmes focus purely on technology and software tools. Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change focuses on the leadership challenge.

Successful adoption of new technologies depends on people. This programme equips leaders with practical approaches for helping teams adapt, engage, learn, and perform during periods of transformation.


About the Facilitators

Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths

This programme combines deep expertise in change leadership and AI transformation. Cat Moody and Jarred Griffiths bring practical experience supporting public sector organisations through organisational change, workforce transitions, leadership development, and AI adoption.

Participants will benefit from real examples, lessons learned, and practical insights drawn from current, hands-on work across public sector agencies.

Live reading of The Black Woman of Gippsland play
Join us at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library for a live reading of The Black Woman of Gippsland by Andrea James. This event will be held in Ngā Pou Ruahine (Level 2), Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library.

Based on real events and set on Andrea’s grandmother’s country, The Black Woman of Gippsland is a poetic, emotionally rich and clever embracing of First Nations stories that have long been silenced. In 2026, Andrea's play The Black Woman of Gippsland was awarded Nick Enright Prize for Playwriting at the NSW Literary Awards, with judges praising it as an outstanding and extraordinary work that deftly reveals how colonial myths shape the way histories are recorded and believed.

This event is part of the Breaking Ground: International Indigenous Writing Festival, produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Wellington City Council, Creative New Zealand, Hannah Playhouse, Toi Aro and Te Haukāinga.

GÓI BÁNH XUÂN 2027 | Vietnamese New Year Rice Cake Workshop
🧧 GÓI BÁNH XUÂN 2027 | VIETNAMESE NEW YEAR RICE CAKE WORKSHOP

🍃 Wrap a cake, share a story, and celebrate Vietnamese traditions together!

Tết không chỉ là dịp đón năm mới mà còn là lúc gia đình sum vầy, cùng nhau gìn giữ và trao truyền những nét đẹp văn hoá Việt Nam.

Have you ever wondered how traditional Vietnamese rice cakes are made? Or perhaps you miss the familiar feeling of preparing bánh chưng and bánh tét with your family back home?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a hands-on cultural cooking workshop where we come together to discover the stories, traditions and flavours of Vietnamese Lunar New Year.

🌸 WHAT WILL WE EXPLORE?

🍃 Bánh Chưng – Traditional square sticky rice cake, symbolising the Earth and gratitude to our ancestors.

🍃 Bánh Tét – A cylindrical sticky rice cake commonly enjoyed during Tết, particularly in Southern Vietnam.

🍃 Bánh Ú – A pyramid-shaped sticky rice cake wrapped in leaves, representing another beautiful part of Vietnamese culinary heritage.

During the workshop, you will:

🌱 Discover the cultural stories and meanings behind traditional Vietnamese rice cakes.

🌱 Learn about ingredients and traditional wrapping techniques.

🌱 Enjoy a hands-on experience guided by our facilitator, Yung Nguyen.

🌱 Connect with families, friends and community members through food and storytelling.

🌱 Create meaningful memories while helping pass Vietnamese traditions to the next generation.

No cooking experience needed! Whether you're Vietnamese, have children curious about their heritage, or simply love exploring different cultures, everyone is welcome.

📅 EVENT DETAILS

Date: Saturday, 16 January 2027

Venue: Te Mako Naenae Community Centre, Lower Hutt

Facilitator: Yung Nguyen

Organiser: Viet Hub NZ

🎟️ Spaces are limited. Registration is essential.

💛 MORE THAN JUST A COOKING WORKSHOP

For many Vietnamese families living overseas, the scent of sticky rice, the sound of leaves being folded and the joy of preparing food together bring back precious memories of home.

For our younger generation, this is an opportunity to discover where they come from, connect with their roots and create their own Tết memories.

And for our wider New Zealand community, it's an invitation to experience the warmth, stories and traditions of Vietnamese culture.

Because traditions are not only something we remember. They are something we share, practise and pass on.

Come wrap a cake, share a story and welcome Tết 2027 with us! 🧧

The Rescue Water Craft (RWC) commonly known as a Personal Water Craft (PWC) or Jetski is specially outfitted for surf interaction and operated by experienced Surf Lifeguards.

As the operator of a Rescue Water Craft you are responsible for the safety of your crew, the public and yourself. It is important that you understand the risks inherent in operating this type of equipment and your role in assessing and minimising risk.

The qualification has a number of theoretical and practical components such as driving in the surf, patient pick up and maritime regulations to prepare experienced Surf Lifeguards for RWC use.

Prerequisites:

Current & active member of a SLS club
Surf Lifeguard Award (Refreshed)
20 years of age minimum on the first day of the introductory course.
Radio Communication Module or Maritime VHF Operator's Certificate
Senior Lifeguard Award - IRB Driver (Refreshed)*
Surf First Aid (Refreshed)**
400m Pool swim under 7.30 minutes
*A minimum of 2 years from IRB Award including 2 seasons operating as a IRB driver is required (at a minimum one IRB driver refresher must have been completed in the last year)
**An RWC Operator must hold a Surf First Aid prior to attending their RWC exam.

Link to more information and the application form is in the comments.

long_description:
Old Jail Museum Open Day
Did you know Petone was the first place in New Zealand to have a Police force? Find out about this and other interesting Petone stories in the Old Jail Museum.

Come to the Old Jail Museum – a well-preserved former lockup. See an exhibition on Policing in Petone from 1840. Read about Jackson Street's heritage, plus various Petone stories, including our rich sporting history. It has information on Jackson Street businesses, directories, Petone walking tours, kids activity sheets, and more to take away.
Either our Heritage Office or a JSP Ambassador will be onsite.
Built in 1908 on Elizabeth Street, it was once the most senior Police Station in the Hutt Valley with ten constables and one sergeant. In the early 1950s, the Police Station and lockup (jail) were moved behind the old courthouse at 13 Elizabeth Street. Police used the courthouse as an office, but the lockup continued to be used – mainly for intoxicated offenders until 1978.


Cost: Free entry; koha is welcomed.

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/old-jail-museum-open-day-26/

This Department of Conservation campsite is part of the Remutaka Forest Park and situated on the road from Wainuiomata to the coast.

Grab a free coffee and chat with other parents and carers who know what it’s like to care for a disabled child, a neurodivergent child, or a child with health impairments.


Parent to Parent hosts regular Parent Support Groups in Upper Hutt to support carers and parents just like you. These groups are a safe space for family and whānau to share their experiences, their challenges, their triumphs, and to learn from each other in an open and 100% judgement-free environment. No topic is too ‘weird’, no question too ‘out there’. We get it, and we are here to help.

Feel free to just show up on the day!

This one’s different.

We’re trading our usual Thursday evening for a Sunday afternoon, swapping the city for Porirua, and stepping courtside with the Tokomanawa Queens.

Women of Pōneke is heading to Te Rauparaha Arena for an afternoon of kōrero, kai, community — and live basketball. Never watched a game in your life? Great! This is your invitation!

Here’s the afternoon:

🥂 Welcome bubbles on arrival

🍽️ Kai and time to connect

This is the team that made history. The Tauihi league launched with pay equity from day one, the first professional women’s sport in New Zealand to do so. The Queens won the first-ever title. The Christmas Tui Express
Christmas should feel like a genuine celebration, and this year you can enjoy it aboard a train journey that is truly unforgettable. Due to huge demand, we are running a second Christmas Tui Express trip, giving friends, families, social groups, and festive adventurers another chance to enjoy this full day scenic rail experience.

Step into our premium carriages and settle in for a relaxed, cheerful journey through some of the lower North Island’s most beautiful landscapes. With great company, stunning views, and a festive onboard atmosphere, the whole day feels like a Christmas treat.

From the open air viewing platform, breathe in the crisp gorge air and capture photos that look straight out of a travel magazine. It is a rare experience and one of the most memorable parts of the journey.

Your celebration begins the moment you board. Our licensed café carriage serves alcoholic and non alcoholic drinks, coffee, and sweet treats throughout the day, making it easy to relax as the scenery rolls by.

🍻 Destination: Tui Brewery
Once we arrive at Mangatainoka Station, enjoy a gentle 15 minute walk or hop on one of our transfer buses to the iconic Tui Brewery.

Your ticket includes a hearty BBQ lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage, with a non-alcoholic alternative available if you prefer. It is the perfect way to toast the festive season and enjoy the laid back Mangatainoka atmosphere before the return journey home.
